turns.learner: Hello! Can you give me an exercise on much and many?
turns.tutor:
I'll think aloud with one: "How ___ oranges are in the box?"
First I ask: can I count oranges? Yes: one orange, two oranges, three oranges. When I can count them, I use many.
Result: How many oranges are in the box?
Rule: many goes with things you can count; much goes with things you can't count.
Right: How much money do you need?
Wrong: How many money do you need?
Now you. Write much or many:
How ___ bottles are there?
